decisions.decision: Split the monolithic Block Contract into seven linked records: CapabilityContract, PackagingProfile, HostContract, BindingPlan, QualificationDossier, RegistryRecord, ReleaseManifest.
decisions.rationale: The seven concerns have seven owners changing on seven different clocks. Fusing them lets a proof re-run mutate the semantic interface a composer reads.
decisions.separation_rule: A field belongs to the record whose owner can change it without invalidating the others.
alternatives_rejected: Keep one contract and document ownership in prose — prose does not prevent the mutation
Split into two (semantic vs evidence) — leaves packaging, host, binding and registry fused
decisions.falsifier: F-SPLIT: a composition is planned from a monolithic contract without the composer reading proof or rights fields

decisions.decision: Carry TWO shape axes, not one: reuse_shape (10 values, architecture) and rights_exposure (4 values, restating S1-S4).
decisions.rationale: Three prior artifacts used three shape vocabularies that were not synonyms. S1-S4 measure how much source is copied (rights/maintenance); the others measure what the module is in the product (architecture). An intact_service copies nothing; a transplant copies source. Merging would have silently deleted the rights-exposure axis.
alternatives_rejected: Merge into one enum and treat the difference as naming drift — loses an axis
Keep three vocabularies — guarantees cross-lane divergence
decisions.falsifier: Two modules share a reuse_shape and a rights_exposure yet need materially different rights handling

decisions.rationale: P03 measured the decisive supply distinction: across 13 case/workflow rows, 7 runnable products exist and every one is copyleft or open-core — clean permissive products: zero — while the permissive candidates (flowable, jBPM) are engine libraries with no UI, identity or workflow. P03 revised this claim twice; collapsing engine and product is the error it caught.
decisions.falsifier: A clean permissive case/workflow product is found, collapsing Trace C

decisions.rationale: Rights work on an unpinned source is wasted because the finding cannot be bound to specific bytes. The Phase 7 corpus records immutable_commit_or_tag NOT_CAPTURED and URLs not independently resolved — it is a nomination layer.
decisions.falsifier: A rights receipt is successfully bound to an unpinned source

decisions.decision: Default donor_settings_policy to donor_rendered_behind_host_nav for v1; treat full remount as a research bet.
decisions.rationale: After a deliberate 33-surface commercial sweep, ZERO render a third party's settings inside host-owned chrome. Zoho One and Microsoft 365 unify at identity and admin and explicitly do not suppress donor chrome. Absence of evidence after a deliberate sweep is not proof of impossibility, but it is not an engineering estimate either.
alternatives_rejected: Promise a unified settings surface in v1 — no precedent to copy
Mark settings absorption impossible — the sweep does not support that either
decisions.falsifier: F-SETTINGS: one donor's settings render in host chrome with full parity and survive a donor upgrade

decisions.decision: Track the host absorption question as three tiers (identity strong / navigation partial / settings none) rather than one `unknown`.
decisions.rationale: A34 conflates three tiers with very different precedent strength and cost class. Identity has 4 independent commercial forms plus a protocol-proven local spike; navigation has two proven halves; settings has nothing.

decisions.decision: The host navigation registry is build-not-adopt.
decisions.rationale: Luigi has the declarative node structure (~45 params, runtime-resolving children, visibleForFeatureToggles, userSettingsGroup) but no contribution model. Backstage has decentralized contribution but emits a React element welded to its own CLI and webpack. Two proven halves, no whole.
decisions.falsifier: A donor contributes nav declaratively at runtime to an adopted registry, gated by role and entitlement

decisions.decision: Tenant isolation is owned, tested work; no dependency removes it.
decisions.rationale: For a TypeScript host there are effectively no adoptable multi-tenancy frameworks. The maintained ones are language-locked (archtechx/tenancy Laravel 4.4k; citusdata/django-multitenant 822); targeted searches otherwise returned sub-5-star templates. NS-TENANT-01 is the only surgery marked recoverable:false.

decisions.decision: Place the host idempotency layer INSIDE the rate limiter and auth check.
decisions.rationale: Stripe's rate limiters run BEFORE its idempotency layer, so a 429 under the same key can produce a different result; the same holds for a 401 with a missing key and most 400s. Copying the ordering reproduces the hazard at Actionist's boundary. Whether to cache failure responses is flagged as a deliberate Actionist decision, not an inherited default.
decisions.note: P11 recorded correcting its own draft invariant here — Stripe caches failures too. The correction is preserved rather than smoothed.

decisions.decision: Refuse registry projection for modules whose rights_state is ambiguous or incompatible.
decisions.rationale: Great Library license.status has 3 values and cannot represent the two states that must block reuse. Projecting them as `pending` erases a rights refusal.
alternatives_rejected: Project as pending and annotate — the annotation is not what a consumer reads
Widen the Great Library enum — not this lane's authority

decisions.decision: Rollback enumerates eight object kinds; the composition horizon is the MINIMUM across objects, computed at release time.
decisions.rationale: Derived twice independently — vendor documentation (Vercel does not revert env vars or configuration; Fly does not revert fly.toml, secrets or migrations) and SISOCRM's operated standard ('Data rollback is separate'), which names a third object no vendor surfaced: a standing alternate UI route. RollbackPlan cannot be a boolean.

decisions.decision: Full repo-to-module automation is rejected; three decisions require a named human.
decisions.rationale: Reuse shape (converts a dependency-update problem into a permanent fork if wrong), migration authority (a product-architecture decision), and admission (implementation_authorized is const:false — not a default, a constant). Automation's deliverable is cheap elimination plus a clean decision packet.
decisions.falsifier: F-DET: shape and migration authority decided mechanically at parity with a named human across ten donors

decisions.decision: Require a shape_decision receipt carrying rejected alternatives.
decisions.rationale: Models are best at exactly the SEMI work — 17 of 28 surgeries. The trap is that SEMI output LOOKS like DET output: a proposed shape and a computed digest are both a short confident string. A shape with no recorded alternatives is not a decision, it is a default nobody noticed.

decisions.decision: Do not publish an adaptation-cost percentage. Publish the categories and their determinism/cost distribution instead.
decisions.rationale: A07 stays unknown. Measured distribution: 3 of 28 surgeries are cosmetic, 13 boundary, 12 architectural; 6 are irreversible. The line-count delta may be small while the boundary delta is not. The framework's contribution is making 'small in lines, large in boundary' plannable, not estimating it.
alternatives_rejected: Quote 1-2% from the operator's observation — it is an observation about line count, not boundary
decisions.falsifier: F-COSMETIC: a representative absorption measures >80% of adaptation hours in cosmetic surgeries

decisions.decision: Accept S2-L4 defect P04-L4-001: port-level external_effect is authoritative over the authority_class summary.
decisions.rationale: L4 identified that a module classed read_only may declare a port whose external_effect is not none, and named it the single most likely place for a silent privilege bug. Stricter wins; the disagreement returns UNDERDETERMINED rather than resolving silently. The class-to-session-ceiling mapping stays owned by L4 so there is one truth, not two.

contradictions_carried.statement: The forge/judge pipeline is described as a gate but has no numeric threshold; blessing is a human act. Automated visual gating is not established.
An AGPL-3.0 donor is operated as a mounted fork while harvest policy classes AGPL as reference-only. Both are current practice.
contradictions_carried.condition: Holds only if intact_service/intact_fork is accepted as a distribution-distinct shape. If a qualified reviewer rejects that distinction, the packaging axis must be rebuilt.
contradictions_carried.owner: named legal reviewer, not this lane

contradictions_carried.statement: The knowledge spine lists 8 reuse shapes; this framework carries 10 (adding intact_fork and reference_only).
contradictions_carried.action: The spine should adopt the 10 or state why 8.

contradictions_carried.statement: L4's `stage` ceiling maps to no capability class — a capability may be bound but not executed. This family does not model a staged-but-unexecuted binding state.

unknowns_preserved.statement: Real adaptation-cost distribution across the 14 categories.
Whether donor settings can render in host chrome at all.
unknowns_preserved.next: Loop 3; must precede any client-facing settings-unification claim

unknowns_preserved.note: An unmeasured cost is BLOCKED, not zero. No estimate is offered.

unknowns_preserved.statement: Whether a permissive CMMN/BPMN engine exists on Node, or whether Trace C must pay a JVM sidecar boundary.
Whether the deterministic elimination layer materially reduces model error and tokens.
